 Meta Stock Down 21%: Too Much AI Spending?
 Trefis Team Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:10 PM CST 3 min read META -6.16% 
 AMZN -4.26% 
 MSFT -2.93% 
 NVDA -13.06% 
 SNAP -11.13%

 Learn more Image from Pixabay Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%? 
 Meta closed at $616.38 on Wednesday. That is 21% below $777.59, its highest close of the past year, reached on Sep 24. Its ads business keeps growing. Analysts expect earnings of $34.14 a share next year, up from $29.09 this year. 
 So what is holding the stock back? The size of its AI bill. And unlike Amazon , Microsoft or Alphabet , Meta has no cloud business to rent that computing power to others. 
 Meta is one of five tests for the AI trade in our series, each with a date to watch. The series starts with What 1 Big Trigger Could Make Nvidia Stock Jump By Dec 31? 
 Meta's capital spending was $104.4 billion over the last year, up 66%. Capital spending is money spent on data centers, servers and other long-lasting assets. It took 78 cents of every dollar of cash Meta's business brought in. Two years ago it took 37 cents. All of it has to pay off through ads. 
 Why Is Meta's AI Bill Different? 
 Meta can earn it back only one way. Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet build data centers partly to rent them to other companies. When AI demand is strong, that rent shows up as cloud sales. Meta builds for its own apps. Its payoff has to come from better ad targeting and new products. That takes longer to show and is harder to measure.

 The stock is not expensive. Meta trades at 18.1 times the earnings analysts expect next year. That is close to Alphabet, at 18.8 times. What is missing is proof that the bill will stop growing faster than the business. 
 Meta is already 21% below its high while investors wait for that proof. Holding on is easier when your portfolio falls less than the market. For every dollar its benchmark lost, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio lost about 81 cents on average, holding 30 quality stocks in equal weight. See how HQ held up . 
 What Should Investors Watch? 
 Dec 9: the Fed. A rate hike is widely expected. Higher rates make spending that pays off years from now harder to justify. 
 Late January: Meta's next report, expected then. Watch two numbers: the 2027 spending plan and growth in ad sales. If spending rises less than ads, the worry should ease. If spending jumps again while ad growth stays flat, the worry should deepen. 
 Early February: Alphabet and Amazon. Their spending plans set the tone for all of big tech. Their ad businesses are also the closest match to Meta's. Alphabet's side is in Why Is Alphabet Stock Down 30%? 
 Story Continues To sum up, Meta's AI spending pays off only through ads. It now takes 78 cents of every dollar of cash from operations. In late January, compare spending growth with ad growth. In our view, that gap will decide where the stock goes. 
 If Meta is a large part of what you own, one company's spending choice decides a lot of your result. That is a good reason to think now about how and when you would sell.
